correctness.rationale: Conditioning on Pi(i)=i leaves every nonincident pair exchangeable. The only changed inversion probabilities are (n-i)/(n-1) for pairs ending at i and (i-1)/(n-1) for pairs starting at i, yielding the weighted formula after multiplication by P(Pi(i)=i)=1/n. The ordinary inversion and aggregate formulas follow by specialization and the exact square-sum identity. Exhaustive enumeration through n=9 independently verifies ordinary, conditional, aggregate, and three nonconstant weighted cases.

originality.rationale: The closest complete source found is Pinsky's paper on inversion number conditioned on exactly k fixed points. Its stated results concern fixed-point count and pair-order probabilities under that count conditioning, not conditioning on the specified event Pi(i)=i and not arbitrary weighted inversion scores. Hultman's conjugacy-class framework treats inversion and cycle statistics but not specified fixed-position conditioning, while Diaconis--Evans--Graham study the fixed-point set without inversion scores. Targeted published-record, exact-formula, current-ledger, and prior-ledger searches did not reveal a statement implying the local weighted law. The aggregate covariance is treated only as a corollary, and older permutation-enumeration literature remains an explicit risk.

value.rationale: Fixed points and inversions are canonical Poisson- and Mahonian-type statistics of uniform permutations. The theorem resolves how the location of a pinned fixed point affects the full class of weighted pair-order scores, not merely one aggregate moment. The left-right imbalance law exposes exact central neutrality and decomposes the total fixed-point/inversion dependence into position-resolved contributions, a distinction hidden by conditioning only on the number of fixed points.
